subtopic: TVM / External library integration — BYOC, extern ops
learningObjective: Understand how TVM integrates external kernel libraries (cuBLAS, cuDNN, TensorRT) into a Relax program.
stem: Which statement about how TVM integrates external libraries (e.g., cuBLAS, cuDNN, TensorRT) into a Relax program is correct?

options.text: External library calls are inlined into TensorIR PrimFunc bodies at compile time; the compiler then applies MetaSchedule to tune the library implementation just like any generated code.

TVM's Bring-Your-Own-Codegen (BYOC) and extern-op mechanisms let a Relax op be lowered to an opaque call into a target library instead of a generated PrimFunc; the compiler treats such calls as black boxes at fusion and scheduling time but still tracks shapes/dtypes at the graph level.
TVM cannot call any external library from a compiled Relax program; all compute must be expressed as generated PrimFunc bodies to be executable by the Relax VM.
BYOC only supports CPU targets; GPU external libraries like cuBLAS must be linked at runtime via the host Python interpreter and cannot be encoded into the compiled artifact.

explanation: TVM's BYOC framework and extern-op mechanism allow a Relax op or subgraph to be lowered to an opaque call into a third-party library (cuBLAS, cuDNN, TensorRT, MKL, etc.). The compiler still knows the shape/dtype at the graph level (for verification and downstream layout planning) but does not see the library's internal loops — so the call is a black box for TensorIR-level scheduling and fusion. This coexists with generated PrimFunc code paths, and both can appear in a single compiled artifact.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: BYOC/extern ops give opaque calls with graph-level shape/dtype visibility.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: external calls are not inlined into TensorIR; the library is not a PrimFunc.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: GPU libraries (cuBLAS/cuDNN/TensorRT) are core BYOC targets.

assumptions: Standard TVM Unity BYOC and extern-op flows.
nonImplications: Does not imply external calls always outperform generated kernels; the choice is workload-specific.
Does not imply the BYOC backend has to be a single library; multi-backend dispatch is possible.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses opaque calls with inlined loops.
distractorRationales.D: Wrong claim that BYOC is CPU-only.
